title: Complete revascularization versus culprit lesion only PCI in NSTEMI
summary:
In patients with myocardial infarction in whom there is no clear indication of a completely occluded infarct vessel in the ECG and in whom coronary multivessel disease is diagnosed, it is unclear according to the current state of scientific knowledge what the optimal treatment is. Either only the infarct vessel is treated or additionally all other relevant obstructed blood vessels of the heart are treated.
The aim of this study is to investigate whether the treatment of the infarct vessel alone is superior over treatment of all other obstructed coronary blood vessels in addition to the infarct vessel.

interventions.name:
Culprit-lesion-only revascularization.
The Culprit-lesion is treated directly as part of the diagnostic cardiac catheterization or in a further cardiac catheterization. Revaskularisation of all Non-culprit-lesions is not planned.

Multivessel revascularization of all significant obstructed coronay vessels.
The Culprit-lesion is treated directly as part of the diagnostic cardiac catheterization or in a further cardiac catheterization. Non-culprit-lesions would be treated either
- during the index procedure,
- the index hosp

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• NSTEMI as suggested by high-sensitivity troponin algorithms
• Multivessel coronary artery disease
• Identifiable culprit lesion
• Informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Cardiogenic shock
• Sustained ventricular tachycardia (VT) or ventricular fibrillation (VF)
• Contraindication for coronary revascularization
• Prior coronary artery bypass graft
• Indication for coronary artery bypass graft surgery
• Co-morbidity with life expectancy less than 6 months
• Type 2 myocardial infarction
